chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, said:

Abu al-Hasan al-Akhir عليه السلام said: Beware of sleeping between Salat al-Layl and al-Fajr; rather, a brief lying down without sleep. For indeed, its practitioner is not praised for what he has sent ahead of his prayer.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الْأَخِيرُ: a title referring to the later Imam known as Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام
key_terms.النَّوْمَ: sleep, specifically sleeping in the interval mentioned
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: the dawn time or Fajr prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةِ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer performed before dawn
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his prayer, referring to the worship already performed
key_terms.ضَجْعَةً: a brief lying down or reclining

ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to sleep between Salat al-Layl and the Fajr prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith discourages sleeping between Salat al-Layl and the Fajr prayer, while allowing a brief recline without actual sleep. It reflects the etiquette and spiritual care connected to night worship and preserving the state of devotion until the morning prayer.
